close_reason: Extracted the dispatcher's createdIds-extraction loop to a private helper fn extract_created_ids_into(primary: &Value, sink: &mut HashMap<Id, Id>) placed next to the JmapHandler trait doc that specifies the response contract. The dispatcher loop becomes a one-liner that calls the helper; the silent-skip behaviour (entries without a string 'id' field) is now auditable in one place rather than inlined in the hot dispatch path. The lower-cost alternative path from the bead was chosen over the typed-HandlerOutcome reshape because the latter is a breaking API change that propagates to every extension *-server crate; that more invasive reshape can be filed separately if a workspace major bump is planned.
description:
What is awkward: crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:189-205 re-introspects primary_value.get("created").and_then(|v| v.as_object()) to extract creationId → id mappings AFTER the handler has produced its response Value. The dispatcher thus has implicit knowledge of the /set response shape, encoded as serde_json::Value navigation rather than a typed return.

The HandlerFuture return type today is Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>. The dispatcher reaches into the Value to find the 'created' key. The handler authoring contract (JmapHandler doc comment, lib.rs:55-61) says: 'Handlers for /set methods … that create objects MUST include an "id" field (type string) in each entry of the "created" map.' — a textual contract enforced by ad-hoc JSON navigation.

Suggested rewrite: change HandlerFuture to Result<HandlerOutcome, JmapError> where:
    pub struct HandlerOutcome {
        pub primary: Value,
        pub extra: Vec<Invocation>,
        pub created_ids: Vec<(Id, Id)>,   // (creation_id, server_id) pairs
    }
Generic /set handlers in handlers.rs populate created_ids explicitly; non-/set handlers pass an empty Vec. The dispatcher iterates created_ids without re-parsing the Value. Two wins:
  (a) the contract is now in Rust types, not in a paragraph of docstring.
  (b) the silent-skip path (lib.rs:198-202: 'Entries without an "id" field are silently skipped — the dispatcher cannot produce an error for a method call that already succeeded') goes away entirely — there's no map to skip from.

Cost: breaking API change to the JmapHandler trait, which propagates to every extension *-server crate. The reshape is mechanical (Ok((value, vec)) → Ok(HandlerOutcome::new(value).with_extra(vec))) but touches 8+ crates per workspace AGENTS.md canonical-template rule. Not free.

Lower-cost alternative: keep the trait shape, but extract the .get("created").iter into a dedicated helper fn extract_created_ids(primary: &Value, sink: &mut HashMap<Id, Id>) and move it next to the handler doc contract. The navigation is still ad-hoc but it lives in one place; the dispatcher reads better.
title: Dispatcher createdIds-extraction uses get("created").and_then.iter pattern that re-reads the response after handler returned
